receipts.claim: A count-only scan of this host's Claude Code transcripts (the 4,183 transcript files that record a version were written by Claude Code 2.1.280 to 2.1.284; scanned 2026-09-29, ccusage 20.0.26), deduplicated by message.id, covers 186,492 API calls and 1,872 advisor iterations from 2026-09-24 to 2026-09-29 (UTC dates). Its input, output, cache-read and cache-creation (5m plus 1h split) totals each match `ccusage claude daily --json --offline`, run on the same copy of the transcript tree, within 0.001%; the top-level cache_creation_input_tokens field is 2.3% higher because of tokens with no split. At Anthropic API list prices the window is $20,927 (ccusage: $19,829; the $1,098 difference is mostly claude-sonnet-5-5, which ccusage leaves unpriced, plus unsplit cache writes only the scan prices, per data.reconciliation.cost_usd): children (Agent-tool and workflow stages) are 81.3% of it, workflow stages alone 66.1%, and 4 of 710 session trees cover half; in ccusage's session view the 303 workflow runs are 68.1% of its dollars (median run $22, largest $448). Cache reads are 39.5% of dollars, executor output 23.8%, cache writes 22.8%, advisor iterations 14.0%. Children with more than 60 calls are 53.2% of dollars; children of a default agent type are 63.4% of children and 41.1% of dollars; effort max covers 82.2% of calls.
limitations: Local observation of one host's retained transcripts (the independent-observation class of docs/acceptance-evidence-policy.md), not a provider ledger or a bill. Both tools read one copy of the transcript tree taken at data.reconciliation.snapshot_at_utc, so their differences are method differences, not drift; a transcript that was deleted or never written is not counted, and the scan skips a line cut by the copy.

The transcripts were written by more than one Claude Code release (data.scan.client_versions_by_transcript_file, 151 files without a version field); the scan and ccusage ran with the versions in data.tool_versions.

Dollar figures apply Anthropic API list prices (data.prices, pricing page fetched 2026-09-29) to counted tokens. They are not what a subscription charges and do not weight the plan meter. Cache-write tokens with no 5m/1h split are priced at the 5-minute rate, and tokens of models absent from the table (data.scan.unpriced_model_tokens) are not priced. The scan-minus-ccusage difference of $1,098 is the sum of the per-model differences in data.reconciliation.cost_usd.by_model: claude-sonnet-5-5 ($1,006, which ccusage leaves unpriced), claude-opus-4-8 (-$6: ccusage prices it and the scan does not) and the unsplit cache writes of the other models ($96, which ccusage does not count), with a residual of $1 that is not attributed.

Counts only: no path, session identifier or transcript content is retained. A session tree is a main session plus every child below it, derived from the path layout; ccusage lists each workflow run as its own session, so its per-session ranking differs from data.scan.session_trees.

Invocation counts are attempts, not success rates: each tool population has its own denominator (data.scan.tool_calls, mcp_calls_by_server), and a ToolSearch load is not a call. No per-tool eligible-task success rate follows from them.

Cache creation: ccusage counts the 5m and 1h split (965,565,309 tokens) and the scan's split matches it. The scan also reports the top-level field (987,672,811 tokens), which is 22,098,490 tokens above the split; after clamping calls whose split exceeds their top-level field to no remainder, the unsplit remainder is 22,133,575 tokens on 1,878 calls (children: 21,760,880 tokens on 1,760 calls; 1 main-session call reports a split larger than its top-level field). Which cache class the remainder belongs to is not established, and the scan prices it at the 5-minute rate. In the split fields children show no 1-hour-class tokens (their unsplit remainder has no established class); main sessions show 142,720,261.

Inference with no usage record is in neither the scan nor ccusage: session titles, compaction, WebFetch summaries, away summaries and the auto-mode classifier. Advisor inference is counted from usage.iterations only. Rows whose model is <synthetic> carry no usage and are skipped.

Cache-miss events (data.scan.cache_misses, cache_creation_children) are calls whose cache read fell below half the previous call's context. The gap is measured between the first-written entries of consecutive calls, so it includes the next call's response time (long at effort max), and calls after a compaction also meet the rule; the 5m-1h bin is therefore approximate.

The scan's rules (one row per message.id with the per-field maximum, advisor iterations, <synthetic> rows and journal files skipped, the --since filter for calls and tool counters) were checked on a synthetic fixture with hand-computed expected values and one mutant run per rule (data.control). The fixture does not check the price table or the run-shape statistics, and the reconciliation covers token totals, not dollars.

The run-shape statistics describe this host and window. They do not show that fewer or shorter children lower cost at equal quality, and data.derived is arithmetic on generic price ratios; no quality comparison was run.

receipts.claim: On this host on 2026-09-29 (Claude Code 2.1.285, and 2.1.283 in a second distro; tmux 3.4; Windows Terminal 1.24.11911.0) the installed client knows 17 distinct notification types, all valid matcher values (a 15-item base array plus the two elicitation completion types), the same 17 in 2.1.283, 2.1.284 and 2.1.285; 12 are documented in the hooks reference. 8 now ring through the overlay's bell hook and 9 stay quiet, each with a reason in one table that the scan and the repository's test share; none is without a decision. The type the bell missed was `push_notification`, the model's own PushNotification. In an interactive pty probe with no user-scope settings a model push raised one Notification event of that type and rang nothing; with one more hook that matches the type, exactly one BEL reached the terminal; and with this host's own settings after the change, the same one BEL. The tool sends only while the client judges the user away: the probe's arms show both branches of the rule read from the binary (with a focus-out report the event fires whatever the elapsed time; with no focus report it fires after more than 60 s without input and does not fire after 15 s); once a focus report has arrived its last state decides, so a tab last reported focused counts as present however long the user is away, and how Windows Terminal reports a background tab was not measured. Before the change, the same probe on this host's settings gave one event and no BEL (the coordinator's own output, recorded as values). Both Claude settings files (this host's and the second distro's) were brought to the overlay with the repository's merge tool on a private copy, backed up, and differ from their originals only in the bell group; a rerun of the hardened replacement tool reports nothing to do on both. The scan's first catalog pattern read 15 of the 17 matcher values on 2.1.283 without an error (a `$` in a minified name); the reader now reads 17 on all three releases, exits 1 when it finds nothing, and the fix is covered by tests and negative controls. tmux 3.4 forwards a pane's BEL to the outer terminal (a pty in the probe) by default, and `bell-action none` or `visual-bell on` stops it.
limitations: One workstation, one probe model (Haiku) and one Ubuntu 24.04 distro plus a second distro (the independent-observation class of docs/acceptance-evidence-policy.md). No audible bell in Windows Terminal was observed by the user in this work, and the probe's outer terminal is a Python pty, not Windows Terminal: Windows Terminal defines DECSET 1004 focus reporting (microsoft/terminal v1.24.11911.0 DispatchTypes.hpp L541), but whether it reports focus for a background tab or an unfocused window, and what the last report is when a real user walks away, was not measured.

The presence rule is read from the installed client, not run against a real absence (`function V4r`, called only by the PushNotification tool: the terminal's focus state is undefined until the first focus report and then the last reported state decides; before any report, input within 60 seconds (`var KWt=60000`); `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NOTIFICATION_PRESENCE_CHECK` bypasses it). The probe measures both branches with a synthetic focus-out report or none. A tab last reported focused counts as present however long the user is away, so the bell can stay silent for a user who left a focused tab; in a terminal session the permission prompt's notification is timed by inactivity (source read: the terminal path compares the time with the later of the prompt's appearance and the last interaction; the fixed-delay timer is the Agent SDK path). Two more conditions leave the bell silent and were read from the binary, not run: with Remote Control connected and `agentPushNotifEnabled` off the tool returns `config_off` before it raises the event, and the tool exists only where the server-side flag `tengu_kairos_push_notifications` is on (it is on for this account).

The probe does not record the tool's reply, so the "Not sent because you're active in this terminal." text (`disabledReason: user_present`) comes from the binary. A headless `-p` run of a few seconds (the elapsed time was not recorded) raised no Notification event and the tool's result began "Not sent"; the same presence rule applies to `-p`, and a longer run was not measured.
The probe cannot say how often a model chooses to send a push, so the decision's overturn condition (models over-notify) is the check.

The 'before' run on this host's own settings (one event, no BEL) is the coordinator's own output of the same probe, recorded here as values; it cannot be repeated now that the live matcher changed. Arms A and B reproduce the same causal pair independently of any user setting. receipts.claim: On this host on 2026-09-29 (Claude Code 2.1.284, bubblewrap 0.9.0, Windows Terminal 1.24.11911.0): a login shell started the way the Windows Terminal profiles start it (wsl.exe --exec /bin/bash -lc) could not find claude, codex or rtk while an empty ~/.bash_profile hid ~/.profile; the empty file had been created within about a second of 14 other empty entries (13 in the home directory, one in the system temp directory) by a scrub-mode `claude -p` probe of a peer session, and removing that one file restored the commands. In an isolated home with the installed client, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 created an empty ~/.bash_profile and removed ~/.local/bin from the login PATH; the same run without the variable created no empty files; and a real ~/.bash_profile that hands off to ~/.profile stayed byte-identical and kept the PATH. The doctor's login-shell-path check failed on the three broken temporary homes and passed on the two healthy ones and on the real host, and the real host's login PATH was identical before and after the hand-off file was created. The reproduction was re-run after the bounded re-check with the client's temporary state redirected to a short private directory beside each throwaway home (TMPDIR and CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR): the real /tmp and /tmp/claude-<uid> gained no top-level entry during the recorded run apart from /tmp/inline-comments-buffer.jsonl, which was absent before, appeared during the run and was removed by the script, the real home's placeholder names were unchanged, and the arm counts were 0 empty files with no variable, 27 with it in the stock home and 26 with a real hand-off file. A control run whose socket path (121 bytes, from a 99-byte private path) exceeded the client's own 103-byte cap on `<dir>/cc-socks/<pid>.sock` put the messaging-socket directory into a fixed /tmp/cc-socks-<uid> directory in the real /tmp instead, so the redirect holds only while the private path is short (under about 81 bytes with a 7-digit pid) and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR stays unset. The native `claude doctor` warned 3 times with the sandbox off and 4 times with it enabled and a planted stale mask file; it named the planted file (the warning is live) and named the scrub-created ~/.bash_profile, a writable 0644 file outside the warning's documented scope of 0-byte read-only placeholders, in neither run. The upstream landscape on 2026-09-29 gave no trigger to change the terminal settings: no new Windows Terminal release, both toast signals unchanged, Claude Code 2.1.284 still the newest, and Codex's notification, palette and kind sources identical between the installed tag and the newest stable tag (rust-v0.159.0 at the re-run).
limitations: One workstation and one Ubuntu 24.04 distro (the independent-observation class of docs/acceptance-evidence-policy.md). The second distro's two per-project Claude profiles were not measured (that distro was later unregistered). Another host collects its own evidence.

The incident's creator is established by timing, by the same-second leftovers in the probe's scratch working directory (present in its scrub arm, absent in its no-scrub arm), by the owning session's confirmation, and by the isolated reproduction plus public reports (anthropics/claude-code #76236, #78072). The peer probe itself was not re-run. The reproduction stops at the API-key check: it shows the files are created at startup, and says nothing about a full session or about exit. Upstream states the placeholders persist after exit and is considering cleaning them up; that was not measured here.

The observations of the incident (login probes before and after, the leftover list, the journal and unit checks) are the coordinator's own shell output of 2026-09-29, recorded here as values; no raw output is retained.

The hand-off file protects only the name ~/.bash_profile. A creator that truncates or replaces an existing file is not covered; the doctor check catches an empty ~/.bash_profile or ~/.bash_login and any missing command, but the doctor has no scheduler, so it finds a recurrence only when it is run.

The doctor code lives in a repository with no remote (practice repository commit 512c3e3); this receipt's artifact folder carries a copy of the function with the home made a parameter. The full doctor run predates the creation of the hand-off file; the check alone was re-run after it.

The Codex comparison is a source diff of four files between two tags plus a check of the notification definitions; Codex 0.159.0 (the newest stable at the re-run) was not run. The candidate notifiers were compared by repository head and latest release only, not run. The three candidates agent-deck, ccmanager and zellij were first recorded by the refresh script on 2026-09-29, so their heads have no earlier pin to be compared with.

The reproduction and the five controls are isolated fixtures (synthetic class); the incident probes and the real-host runs are native observations. Entry counts of the reproduction varied by one between runs of the same script (50 entries in the stock-home arm in the first run, 49 in the re-runs); the conclusions rest on the booleans and the empty-file counts. The native `claude doctor` was run in one throwaway home with the scrub-created file, with the sandbox off and with it enabled plus a planted stale mask file. That planted file shows the warning is live; it is not a positive control for the scrub placeholder, which the warning's documented scope (0-byte read-only placeholders at settings paths) does not cover, so the doctor's silence about ~/.bash_profile follows from that scope and is not evidence about the file.

The `claude agents --json` figures are a live snapshot of this host's sessions at the time of the run; the same command with a path that holds no session printed no rows, and `--all` added one completed background session.

The private temporary directory changes where the client's temporary state goes, not what it creates in the home or the working directory, and it holds only while it is short: the client caps its messaging-socket path, <dir>/cc-socks/<pid>.sock, at 103 bytes (its own constant), and a private path of 99 bytes, which gives a 121-byte socket path, made it use a fixed /tmp/cc-socks-<uid> directory in the real /tmp (the control run; the client also prefers XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, which the probes never set). That the real /tmp and /tmp/claude-<uid> gained no other top-level entry is a property of the recorded run (about three seconds, on a host where other sessions were running): a concurrent session can add an entry inside that window, and one would have counted. What each arm's private directory held varies a little between runs, so those counts are one run's observation. The shared /tmp/inline-comments-buffer.jsonl sits at a path the client hard-codes; the script cannot tell its own arms' creation of it from a concurrent session's, so it reports that the file appeared during the run and removes it only when it was absent before and is an empty regular file created after the run began.
